external_spec_note: The truncation mechanism and the mul-first ideal ratio are both derivable purely from the two statements themselves plus the fixed integer literals 5/12 and 2/9 already appearing in the buggy code; no protocol/business convention needed.
finding_level_note: Member A (@During, line 141, transfer.arg[0] >= amount*5/12) covers the div-then-mul truncation on the _marketingWalletAddress leg (amount.div(12).mul(5)); Member B (@During, line 142, transfer.arg[0] >= amount*2/9) covers the same truncation on the _dipWalletAddress leg (amount.div(9).mul(2)) -- symmetric halves of the same operator_order_issue finding in sendETHToTeam, both independently Expressible=Yes, same relation form/scope, so a single unioned RQ2-A profile is reported (per the 29_H_08 precedent) rather than two separate breakdowns to sum.
case_notes: SafeMath's `.div()`/`.mul()` order-dependence (floor-division truncates before the subsequent multiply) is load-bearing for both members -- it is exactly why amount.div(12).mul(5) and amount.div(9).mul(2) can fall short of the mul-first ideal amount*5/12 / amount*2/9. Per Step 2 this is a generic, protocol-independent library-semantics fact (identical in any contract using SafeMath), so it is recorded as a case note rather than counted under Additional functions.
extraction_note: Two @During annotations confirmed verbatim from the case JSON, attached at lines 141 and 142 of sendETHToTeam(uint256 amount) respectively (`_marketingWalletAddress.transfer(amount.div(12).mul(5));` and `_dipWalletAddress.transfer(amount.div(9).mul(2));`). relation_form classified as call_argument (each relation directly constrains the value passed into a `.transfer()` call, `transfer.arg[0]`) rather than inequality_bound, per R1-5's explicit call-argument-relation category. Each member's relevant slice is exactly its own target statement -- `amount` is a bare function parameter (no other statement defines it), so no additional same-function context is needed and context_breadth is 0, not 1; relevant_statements is a union count of 2 (one target statement per member), unique_values is a union count of 3 (amount, shared by both members, plus each member's own destination wallet state variable). This is the same shape as WANGMI/Nokon's div-order truncation pattern, so Value-level and During are consistent with those two cases' classification. This is a distinct case_id from numscout_BoostToken_indivisible even though both target the same sendETHToTeam function and same source file family -- the two case JSON files (operator_order_issue/ vs indivisible_amount/) carry different @During annotations for different reported patterns on the same function, each analyzed and recorded independently per its own case JSON.
